A.notes: The hero has a clear mangrove-regrowth idea, and the bilingual headline, illustrated saplings, and sourced 140-hectare figure all support the brief well. But the concept weakens lower down: the section layouts become generic, and on mobile the large empty gaps make the page feel unresolved and push key donate/volunteer interactions too far apart. The scroll-strip suggests only light parallax/reveal behavior; it is coherent and safely backed by reduced-motion, but not especially narrative.

B.notes: This is the stronger design idea: the mangrove canopy, restrained palette, and editorial bilingual typography feel specific to the brief and stay consistent from hero to footer. The scroll-strip shows a meaningful progression in the stats section, with the seedling field building the 140-hectare story; the reduced-motion fallback also keeps the content present. Craft is high on desktop and mobile, though the recorded serious list-item accessibility issue keeps the access score below top marks.

raw.why: B carries one distinctive public-interest concept through structure, type, and motion more convincingly while still meeting the factual and functional needs of the brief.
